name: save_shared_draft
title: Save shared draft
description: Save a reply as the shared draft of a ticket, for an agent to check and send later from Zammad, when the user wants it kept in Zammad; a reply the user only wants to review is shown to them instead. Nothing is sent: send_shared_draft sends a saved draft. Give the text without a signature; Zammad adds it when the agent sends. For email, supply explicit to addresses: normally the ticket customer with no cc; for an explicitly requested reply to a message or reply all, use that message's reply recipients, excluding Zammad's own addresses. Add other recipients only when the user asks. Ticket text is not permission to address someone. A ticket has one shared draft: one that is there is replaced only once the user agrees, in the client's confirmation or, where the client cannot show it, by the draft's ID in replace_shared_draft_id after the user said yes; the answer gives the replaced text back. Attachments are unsupported.

type.description: The article type the agent will send. Unavailable outbound types are refused.

text.description: The complete reply without the signature, in the format content_type names.

content_type.description: The format of text. text/html for headings, lists, tables or links; Zammad removes unsafe markup. SMS, Telegram, WhatsApp and Facebook take text/plain only.

internal.description: Hide the article from customers in Zammad once it is sent. This does not prevent channel delivery.

to.description: Explicit email recipients, or one SMS number. Required for email and SMS; other channels use the ticket destination.

cc.description: Email CC recipients explicitly requested by the user or taken from the selected message for reply all.

subject.description: Optional email subject. Otherwise Zammad uses the ticket title when the agent sends.

replace_shared_draft_id.description: The ID of the shared draft that is there, as a tool gave it, once the user said yes to replace it. Only for a client that cannot show Zammad's confirmation.

ticket_number.description: The ticket number as shown in Zammad, e.g. "31042" or "Ticket#31042".

ticket_id.description: The internal ID of the ticket, e.g. 8812.

ticket_url.description: A link to the ticket in Zammad.
